title_as_printed: Experimental solubility of n-hexane in pure water (mole fraction), this work.

footnotes_as_printed.general: n = number of samples analyzed, x = mole fraction in aqueous phase, sigma_x = ((n x sum x^2 - (sum x)^2)/n x (n-1))^1/2.

pressure_note: P printed per row (about 0.5 MPa); paper does not say whether it is total pressure or what gas (a methane cylinder 'for pressurizing system' and pressurized nitrogen appear in the Fig. 1 legend) sets it; not stated

value.what: mole fraction of n-hexane in the aqueous phase, pure water (salt-free by construction)

uncertainty.what: two standard deviations of the n replicate samples

notes: n-hexane is a liquid hydrocarbon (not one of the seven standard gases); static-analytic method with Rolsi sampler. Whether a hydrocarbon-rich liquid phase is present is not stated explicitly, so regime left empty.
